title: 1959 AHSME Problem 35
statement: The symbol \(\ge\) means “greater than or equal to”; the symbol \(\le\) means “less than or equal to.” In the equation \((x-m)^2-(x-n)^2=(m-n)^2,\) \(m\) is a fixed positive number, and \(n\) is a fixed negative number. The set of values \(x\) satisfying the equation is:

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: the set of all real numbers

solutions.text:
Factoring the left side gives \[ \begin{aligned} &(n-m)(2x-m-n)\\ &\qquad=(m-n)^2. \end{aligned} \] Since \(m\ne n,\) division by \(n-m\) yields \(2x-m-n=n-m,\) so \(x=n.\) This single negative value is not any of choices A through D.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Factor the difference of squares on the left
Because \(m\ne n,\) divide by \(m-n\) and solve for \(x\)
